newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bonds close weaker on U.S. rate speculation.
newsitem.headline: Canada bonds close weaker on U.S. rate speculation.

text.p: Canadian bonds ended weaker on Tuesday as expectations grew that the U.S. Federal Reserve could hike rates as early as this month, analysts said.

"The market has taken this view that potentially there's a bigger chance of Fed tightening than what was believed coming out of Friday's numbers," said Michael Gregory, an economist and strategist with Lehman Brothers. "Canada has basically gone along for the ride."
Canada's 8.0 percent bond due 2023 fell C$0.80 to C$101.75 to yield 7.841 percent. The U.S. 30-year benchmark fell 29/32 to yield 7.02 percent.
The spread between the benchmark bonds narrowed to 82 basis points from 84 points at the close of trading on Monday.

U.S. Treasuries sold off on early in the session after Reuters reported comments from a senior Fed official which aggravated fears of a rate hike. The official told Reuters there is a growing consensus among Fed policymakers that U.S. rates will rise 25 basis points.
In Canada, bonds had weakened earlier in the session following the release of manufacturing data for July from Statistics Canada.

The government agency reported July manufacturers' shipments rose 3.0 percent, new orders rose 3.7 percent and unfilled orders rose 0.7 percent. The numbers were all higher than economists' forecasts.

In new issue news, the Municipal Finance Authority of British Columbia issued a C$100 million, 7.25 percent bond due September 25, 2006. The issue was priced at C$98.81 to yield 7.421 percent with a spread of about 21 basis points over the Government of Canada 8.75 percent bond due December, 2005.
In other prices, the 7.0 percent of 2006 fell C$0.56 to C$97.43 to yield 7.361 percent.
The U.S. 10-year benchmark fell 24/32 to yield 6.83 percent. The spread between the two bonds narrowed to 53 basis points from 55 basis points at Monday's close.
The three-month cash bill traded at 3.81 percent against the U.S. three-month bill at 5.31 percent.
